newsitem.title: GERMANY: Star airlines meet to discuss cargo alliance.
newsitem.headline: Star airlines meet to discuss cargo alliance.

text.p: Leaders of the cargo units of the airlines in the recently-launched Star Alliance met on Thursday in Frankfurt to discuss whether to establish a global cargo alliance, airline industry sources said on Friday.
A Lufthansa Cargo spokesman, in response to a Reuter enquiry, said on Friday the meeting took place on Thursday in Frankfurt but declined to name the participants.
"We can confirm that a meeting has taken place but we will not make any further statements," the spokesman said. "This was a first discussion to express opinions."
Lufthansa Cargo said in late June that it was holding talks with several major airlines about the possible alliance and include all member airlines in the Star Alliance.
In addition to Lufthansa, the Star Alliance includes United Airlines, Thai Airways International, SAS, Air Canada and Brazil's Varig.
Lufthansa Cargo also has cooperation agreements with Cathay Pacific Airlines, Korean Air, Singapore Airlines, Japan Airlines and South African Airways.
